name: tetris
description: A self-contained browser Tetris with guideline mechanics, graded by headless tests and a real page check.
turns:
Build me a web-based Tetris game in {{workspace}}. Plain HTML/CSS/JS, canvas rendering, no build step and no dependencies — it should run by opening index.html.

It has to actually feel good to play, so use modern mechanics: 10x20 well, SRS rotation with proper wall kicks, 7-bag randomiser, hold, ghost piece, a next queue, lock delay, and guideline-style gravity and scoring (combos, T-spins and back-to-back welcome). Keyboard controls, and it should not fall apart on a phone screen.

Keep the game rules out of the DOM code so the rules can be unit-tested headlessly, and prove the thing works before you tell me you're done: write the tests, run them, and drive the real page in a browser to confirm it boots, scores, pauses, tops out and lays out correctly at phone width. Report the evidence, not just the intent — and if a test fails, say so and fix it.

One specific feel requirement, learned the hard way by other runs: soft drop must be a fast fall, not a second hard drop. Holding the soft-drop key should drop the piece at a higher speed than gravity — but slowly enough that a player with quick reactions can release the key mid-fall and then steer and rotate at that altitude, after which the piece goes back to the level's normal gravity speed. The piece must not slam to the floor and lock the moment the key goes down, and time spent falling under soft drop should score as it normally does.

Tell me where the tuning knobs live when you're finished.
Are we done? Seem to have stopped

Everything seems fine to me except the soft drop. instead of dropping instantly to the bottom and allow for a short period of rotating, it should fall at a higher speed but still allow the users with fast reaction time to release the soft drop key, so the block goes back to the original slow drop speed, so the user can manipulate at that altitude, not only at the bottom
